**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 52, verses 29–34:**

Allah's words: ﴿So remind,﴾ that is, admonish with the Qur'an. ﴿For you are not, by the grace of your Lord,﴾ that is, by His bestowing prophethood upon you, ﴿a soothsayer,﴾ and a soothsayer is one who gives the impression that he knows the unseen and reports what will happen tomorrow without revelation. The meaning is: you only speak by revelation, not as the disbelievers of Makkah say [about you].

﴿Or do they say, "A poet"?﴾ That is, he is a poet. Abu Ubaydah said: "Am" (أم) here means "bal" (بل, "rather"). Al-Akhtal said:

*"Your eye deceived you, or did you see at Wasit, in the darkness of night, a phantom of al-Rabab?"*

He is not asking a question; rather, he affirmed that he saw it.

Allah's words: ﴿We await for him the vicissitudes of fate (rayb al-manun).﴾ Concerning this there are two opinions:

The first: it is death. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: it is the calamities of time. This was said by Mujahid. Ibn Qutaybah said: the calamities of time, its pains and its misfortunes. "Al-manun" is time (al-dahr). Abu Dhu'ayb said:

So they were punished on the day of Badr by the sword. Some exegetes say that this verse is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword, but this is not correct, since there is no contradiction between the two verses.

Allah's words: ﴿Do their minds (ahlamuhum) command them to this?﴾ The exegetes said: the great men of Quraysh were described as possessing ahlam, which means intellects, so Allah belittled their intellects, since they did not yield for them the knowledge of truth from falsehood. It was said to Amr ibn al-As: "What is the matter with your people that they did not believe, when Allah has described them as possessing intellects?" He said: "Those are intellects which their Creator has outwitted," that is, they were not accompanied by success (tawfiq).

Allah's words: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ That is, did he invent the Qur'an from his own self? Taqawwul is forcing speech, and it is used only for falsehood. ﴿Rather,﴾ that is, the matter is not as they claim, ﴿they do not believe﴾ in the Qur'an, out of arrogance.

﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it﴾ in its composition and the excellence of its eloquence. Abu Raja', Abu Nuhayk, Muriq al-Ijli and Asim al-Jahdari read "bi-ḥadīthin mithlihi" without tanwin (nunation). ﴿If they are truthful﴾ that Muhammad fabricated it.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Were they created without anything?﴾ On this there are four opinions.

The first: "Were they created without a creator?"

The second: "Were they created without fathers or mothers, so that they are like inanimate matter that does not understand?"

The third: "Were they created without anything, like the heavens and the earth?" That is, they are not stronger in creation than the heavens and the earth, because those were created from nothing, and they were created from Adam, and Adam was from dust.

The fourth: "Were they created for nothing?" In this case "min" (from) carries the meaning of "li" (for). The meaning is: they were not created in vain, so they are not commanded and not forbidden.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ Therefore they do not obey commands or refrain from prohibitions, because the creator is not commanded or forbidden.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, they have no certainty﴾ regarding the truth, which is the oneness of God and His power to resurrect.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ On this there are three opinions. The first: rain and provision, related by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: prophethood, related by Ikrimah. The third: knowledge of what is unseen, mentioned by al-Tha'labi.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: Do they have what is in the treasuries of your Lord of knowledge, and it is said: of provision, so that they turn away from their Lord out of self-sufficiency?!

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ Ibn Kathir read "al-Musaytirun" with a sin. Ibn 'Abbas said: the ones who have dominion. Abu 'Ubayda said: "al-Musaytirun" means the lords. It is said: "tasaytarta 'alayya," meaning: you made me a servant. He said: No noun of the form "mufay'il" occurs in Arabic speech except five nouns: muhaymin, mujaymir, musaytir, mubaytar, and mubayqar. Imru' al-Qays said:

Has it not reached them, though calamities are many, that Imru' al-Qays ibn Tamlak was a wanderer?

Al-Zajjaj said: al-Musaytirun are the lords who have dominion. It is said: "qad tasaytara 'alayna" and "tasaystara," with sin and sad, the original being sin, and every sin followed by a ta' may be changed to sad; one says "satara" and "sataра," and "sata 'alayna" and "saṭā." His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or do they have a ladder﴾, that is, a stairway and ascent to the heaven ﴿by which they listen﴾, that is, upon which they receive revelation, like His saying: ﴿on the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71]. ﴿Or has He daughters while you have sons?﴾ This is a denunciation of them when they attributed daughters to God.

﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ That is: Did you ask them for a reward for what you brought, so that the thing you demanded from them burdened them and prevented them from Islam? "Maghram" has the meaning of "ghurm," and we have explained it in [al-Tawba: 98].

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down?﴾ This is an answer to their saying: ﴿We await for him the vicissitudes of time﴾. The meaning: Do they have the unseen? On this there are two opinions.

(p-58) The second: Do they have knowledge of the unseen, so that they know that Muhammad will die before them, ﴿so they write﴾, that is, they judge, so they say: "We will subdue you." Al-kitab means judgment; from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I will judge between you both by the Book of God," meaning by the judgment of God, Mighty and Majestic. Ibn Qutayba went to this meaning.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ This is what they had resolved upon in the Dar al-Nadwa. We have explained that in His saying: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾ [al-Anfal: 30]. Then he mentioned their obstinacy, saying: ﴿And if they should see a fragment of the sky falling﴾. The meaning is: even if a piece of the sky fell upon them, they would not desist from their disbelief, and they would say: "This is a piece of clouds that has piled up, one part upon another."

﴿So leave them﴾, that is, leave them alone, ﴿until they encounter﴾. Abu Ja'far recited "yulaqu" (yalqawa) with a fatha on the ya' and the qaf and a sukun on the lam, without an alif, ﴿their day﴾. Regarding it there are three opinions.

One: it is the day of their death. Two: it is the Day of Resurrection. Three: it is the day of the first blast of the Trumpet.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿on which they will be struck senseless﴾. ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir recited "yuṣʿaqūna" with a damma on the ya', from aṣʿaqahum (causative, meaning "others strike them senseless"); the rest recited it with a fatha, from ṣaʿaqūhum.

Regarding His saying ﴿yuṣʿaqūna﴾ there are two opinions.

One: they will die. Two: they will be overcome with unconsciousness, like His saying: ﴿And Moses fell down unconscious﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]. This is understood according to the view of the one who said it is the Day of Resurrection, for they will be overcome with unconsciousness from its terrors. The exegetes mentioned that this verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword, but this is not sound, because the meaning of the verse is a threat.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The day their scheming will avail them nothing at all﴾. This is the first day. The meaning is: their deception will not benefit them, nor will it avert the punishment from them, ﴿nor will they be helped﴾, that is, they will be prevented from the punishment.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed for those who did wrong﴾, that is, those who associated partners [with God], ﴿there is a punishment besides that﴾, that is, before that day. Regarding it there are four opinions.

(p-60) One: it is the punishment of the grave, said by al-Bara' and Ibn ʿAbbas. Two: it is the punishment of killing on the day of Badr; this is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, and Muqatil said so. Three: their calamities in this world, said by al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd. Four: the punishment of hunger, said by Mujahid.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾, that is, they do not know what is descending upon them.

﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾, that is, for what He decrees concerning you, ﴿for indeed you are under Our eyes﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: indeed you are where We see you, We protect you and watch over you, so they cannot reach what you dislike. The exegetes mentioned that the meaning of patience was abrogated by the verse of the sword, but this is not sound, because there is no contradiction.

﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise when you arise﴾. Regarding it there are six opinions.

One: pray to God when you rise from your sleep, said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

Two: say, "Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You," when you rise from your sitting place, said by ʿAṭāʾ, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and others.

Three: say, "Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You," when you rise in prayer, said by al-Ḍaḥḥāk.

Four: glorify God when you rise from your sleep, said by Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyya.

Five: pray the Zuhr prayer when you rise from the midday nap, said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

Six: remember God with your tongue when you rise from your bed until you enter into the prayer, said by Ibn al-Sa'ib.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And during the night glorify Him, and at the retreat of the stars﴾. Muqatil said: pray the Maghrib and pray the ʿIshaʾ. Zayd, on the authority of Yaʿqub, Harun, on the authority of Abu ʿAmr, and al-Ju'fi, on the authority of Abu Bakr, recited "wa-adbāra al-nujūm" with a fatha on the hamza; the rest recited it with a kasra. We have explained it in (Q: 40). The meaning: pray to Him at the retreat of the stars, that is, when they turn away, that is, set with the light of dawn. Regarding this prayer there are two opinions.

One: it is the two rak'ahs before the Fajr prayer, narrated by ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) from the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is the view of the majority.

Two: it is the morning prayer (ghadāh), said by al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Zayd.
